perspective:
Arthur Chung’s available information:

- He knows he is Arthur Chung, a plumber with a doctorate, working with Teresa Ortega, a medical assistant colleague, on a community service project. He knows they have collaborated professionally before and he respects her.
- He observes Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed during the project. He feels concerned for her well-being and decides to offer help.
- He hears Teresa say she thinks she can manage but there is a lot to do. He tells her self-care matters and offers to help with tasks so they can finish faster together. Teresa accepts help organizing medical supplies; he agrees to start.
- Arthur believes Teresa is hesitant to accept help because she wants to prove her capability. He feels empathy and wants to reassure her.
- He tells Teresa that accepting help does not mean she is incapable, and that teamwork can be more effective. Teresa says she appreciates it but wants to show she can do it herself; she later agrees she sometimes needs reminding. Arthur says they are in it together.
- Arthur later believes Teresa is still struggling and feels frustrated that his help is not yielding results. He wants another way to support her without making her feel inadequate.
- He tells Teresa he sees things are still tough and that she is doing a great job. Teresa says it has been busy and she feels behind. Arthur proposes working together instead of just helping her; Teresa agrees.
- Arthur feels hopeful that collaboration will ease Teresa’s burden and improve efficiency. He tells her this; Teresa agrees it feels less overwhelming. He proposes handling inventory while she manages patient records, with regular check-ins. Teresa agrees.
- Arthur believes their collaboration strengthened their professional relationship and feels satisfied. He tells Teresa their teamwork paid off. Teresa agrees. He proposes continuing the collaborative approach in future projects; Teresa calls it a fantastic idea and says they are more efficient and effective as a team. Arthur looks forward to their next project; Teresa thanks him for being supportive.

He does not have access to Teresa’s private thoughts or feelings except what she says aloud or what he infers from her behavior.
